articles.title: US announces South Africa visa curbs over race claims
articles.summary: The visa restriction policy targets South African nationals who US Secretary of State Marco Rubio claims are responsible for "race-based discrimination" against white citizens.

image.caption: US President Donald Trump clashed with South African President Cyril Ramaphosa in the Oval Office in May 2025Image: Jim Watson/AFP

blocks.text: The United States has announced a new visa restriction policy for South Africans amid continuing claims that the white, Afrikaner minority in the African country is suffering from "race-based discrimination."

US President Donald Trump's administration has ⁠criticized South Africa over a range of issues including land and employment laws that are meant to redress inequalities that Black people still face 30 years after the end of apartheid.

"As President Trump has made clear, the South African people are being failed by a government that is destroying its economy through an obsessive pursuit of racial grievance against the Afrikaner minority," US Secretary of State Marco Rubio claimed.

"The United States will not allow such behavior to go unchecked," Rubio said. "These actions directly undermine peace, economic stability, and the rule of law, and they are incompatible with the pillars of America's foreign policy."
The US ambassador ‌to South ⁠Africa ⁠said ​​on ​social media ‌on Wednesday that ‌the visa restrictions were "only the first ⁠step ​in ​a ​series of ‌escalatory measures."

Rubio did not name any individuals to be immediately affected by the restrictions but said they would target those who promote "race-based discrimination, incite violence, or enable land confiscation without compensation in South Africa."
South Africa: Discrimination claims based on misinformation

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa says there is no evidence of discrimination against white people in his country and has called for global efforts to debunk ⁠false ​stories about white persecution.
Nevertheless, the Trump administration has continued to attack South Africa.

In 2025, Trump berated President Ramaphosa in the Oval Office over discredited claims of a "white genocide" in South Africa. He has also hit the country with high tariffs, boycotted a G20 summit in Johannesburg and launched a special program allowing thousands of white Afrikaners to settle in the United States.

Relations between Washington and Pretoria have also nosedived over South Africa's genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice (ICJ), in which it accuses the US ally of war crimes and crimes against humanity in the Gaza Strip.

articles.title: Why Romblon’s islands deserve more love and attention
articles.summary: There’s something magical about Tablas, Romblon – even during monsoon season

blocks.text: Listen to this playlist while you read.

The sun was up when we arrived at Tablas Island, offering a stark contrast to Metro Manila’s gloomy August skies. As we made our way to our resort in San Agustin, the coastal highway opened up to endless views of the sea. It’s a sight that stayed with me, making it feel as if the island itself were saying, “This is just the beginning.”
The whole trip felt like a reminder to slow down and surrender to Tablas’ quiet yet inviting atmosphere. And with each minute spent on the island, I found myself wanting for more.

blocks.caption: Tablas Island view 1
Tablas Island view 2

blocks.text: Underrated, laid-back beaches

Before this Sunlight Air-sponsored trip, I’d never heard of Tablas, but Bon Bon Beach is now etched in my memory. The entire journey was filled with similarly unforgettable moments. A standout, however, was Bon Bon Beach itself. Ranked number 38 on the 2025 World’s 50 Best Beaches list, it offered a truly one-of-a-kind experience.

Bon Bon beach stretches long and wide, ending at its northern tip with the famous sandbar that reaches toward Bang-og, a small, uninhabited island. Unfortunately, the high tide kept the sandbar hidden, so we cut short what could have been a ten-minute walk to the far end. Still, the waters on the southern side of the beach were calm and clear enough to swim in.
We also crossed over to Cobrador Island, which had clear, picturesque waters and a laid-back vibe.
Cove Aurelio in Calatrava, on the other hand, was a secluded spot surrounded by towering limestone rock formations that offered an even more intimate escape.

Heading to the far north end of Tablas Island, we visited Lapus-Lapus beach. The name translates to 'tagos-tagos' in Tagalog, as a giant limestone formation in between the shores create an illusion of two completely separate beaches. Walking through them feels like stepping from one hidden cove right to another. A similar vibe awaits at Binucot beach on the southern coast of Tablas.

While clear waters and white sand isn’t so rare in the country, the true charm of Romblon comes from two things. First, we felt so much more connected to the place because, for the most part, we were the only ones exploring the area while the locals simply went on with their day. Secondly, you can’t easily find Romblon food anywhere else but Romblon — and it’s very underrated.
The taste of Romblon

On our way to Odiongan, we asked our guide, Josh Martinez of the Romblon Provincial Tourism Office, about local delicacies we could bring home. His response resonated with me: “‘Yung mga delicacies ng Romblon, hindi siya basta nai-uuwi, you have to experience them here.”
Over the next four days of our stay there, I found out how right he was.

One dish that stood out was Taghilaw, a savory stew of pork meat, innards, and liver simmered in vinegar and water. When I described it later to a friend, he asked if it resembled Bopis. Taghilaw has a similar texture, but with larger cuts of meat. And unlike the sauteed and oily Bopis, Taghilaw is distinctly soupy.

blocks.caption: Romblon Food Spread

blocks.text: On the spread

items: Taghilaw Pork meat, innards, and liver stew simmered in water, vinegar, and spices.
Gayabon Fresh taro leaves cooked in coconut milk.
Steamed Vegetables with Balitsaw Fermented shrimp sauteed in coconut milk, served alongside local greens.
Pinangat nak isra Yellowfin tuna cooked slowly in rich coconut milk.
Crispy fried bolinao Breaded anchovies fried golden for the perfect crunch.

blocks.text: For a healthier choice, Inaslom is Romblomanons’ answer to Northern Luzon’s Dinengdeng or the Tagalog Bulanglang. The locals claimed this dish has at least a hundred variations that every family across the province has its own signature twist.
The version served to us in Odiongan was made with bamboo shoots and corn simmered in a base of hibe (dried shrimp) which filled the dining space with its rich aroma.

blocks.caption: Inaslom dish

blocks.text: As for seafood, the highlight was Sarsa na Uyang (freshwater prawns) over lunch at Cobrador Island. Finely pounded shrimp paste is mixed with shredded coconut, siling labuyo, ginger, garlic, onions, and spices, then wrapped in coconut leaves and boiled in coconut milk. Personally, this would be best enjoyed when topped onto hot, steaming rice.

blocks.caption: Sarsa na Uyang dish

blocks.text: Sarsa na Uyang.

While these dishes had to be enjoyed on the spot, I did manage to bring home packs of Tipin, a circle-shaped, thin yet crunchy coconut biscuit made by the Romblon-native Shapes Bakeshop. My only regret was not buying more, as they are surprisingly addictive.
Romblon Heritage

blocks.caption: Fuerza de San Andres view 1
Fuerza de San Andres view 2
Fuerza de San Andres view 3

blocks.text: To dive into Romblon’s past, we visited one of the twin forts, the Fuerza de San Andres. The forts are located on Romblon Island (an island within the province of Romblon), just a 30-minute motorboat ride away from Tablas.

On the way up the fort, you are greeted by mosaic artworks etched onto the steps. These depict local folklore, including the origin of the province’s name from Dublon or Donblon, and the act of a bird warming an egg in its nest.

blocks.caption: Dublon Mosaic

blocks.text: Built during the Spanish colonial period, Fuerza de San Andres once served as a watchtower to protect the area from Dutch and Muslim invaders. Unfortunately, its twin, Fort Santiago, was destroyed in ruins by Moro pirates centuries ago.

Another notable heritage stop is the San Jose Cathedral. Built in 1644 using limestone, red bricks, and egg-white mortar, this Baroque church is famous for housing the revered image of Nuestra Señora del Sto. Niño de Romblon. You might recognize it from the news, as the centuries-old icon was stolen in 1991 and only returned home in 2013 after more than two decades.
Marble Capital of the Philippines
Romblon is known as the Marble Capital of the country. And true to its title, you’ll see it everywhere – from local roads to the provincial capital itself.

We got a glimpse of where it all begins, mined straight from the hillsides. During an impromptu stop at our guide’s house, we saw for ourselves how common raw marble blocks are, as they had some right in their backyard.

blocks.caption: Backyard raw marble

blocks.text: We visited a local workshop to watch raw marble blocks sliced and polished into sleek floor tiles. Meanwhile, local artisans shape the stone into charming trinkets that we couldn't resist picking up at a pasalubong center in Odiongan.

blocks.caption: Marble trinkets

blocks.text: How to get there
Reaching Romblon used to mean committing to an eight-to-ten-hour journey via ferry, or flying into Caticlan and crossing open waters by boat. But an easier route is offered by Sunlight Air.

Through direct flights from Clark International Airport to Tablas Island, Sunlight Air cuts the trip to at least 1 hour and 15 minutes. For travelers coming from Metro Manila, there are car rental services like Hertz or point-to-point (P2P) buses departing directly from Trinoma in Quezon City.
Pulling you back in
Though the monsoon rain kept us from ticking all the places in our itinerary, it left me with a quiet longing to return under sunny skies.
But missing a few spots is only part of why I want to go back. There’s something rare that Romblon offers to visitors: a tranquil, unhurried escape free from heavy tourist crowds.

Catching Romblon’s islands in shrouded grey skies reminded me that travel isn't just about admiring a destination at its absolute best. It’s about learning to appreciate a place for what it reveals, even when it isn’t postcard-perfect.
Romblon stole my heart – and I’m sure it will steal yours too. – Rappler.com

articles.summary: Former President Rodrigo Duterte appeared in the ICC courtroom ​in The Hague ​dressed in a black suit and ‌white ⁠shirt, for a hearing about his health and ability to stand trial, ​which ​is…

blocks.text: Published September 16, 2026 6:09pm

Former President Rodrigo Duterte appeared in the ICC courtroom ​in The Hague ​dressed in a black suit and ‌white ⁠shirt, for a hearing about his health and ability to stand trial, ​which ​is scheduled ⁠to begin in November.
Duterte, 81, was seated inside the courtroom before the judges arrived, according to a report by GMA News stringer Andy Penafuerte III.
His appearance marked his first in-person attendance at an ICC hearing. On March 14, 2025, he faced the ICC hearing through video conferencing.
The former president has been detained at the ICC since his transfer to The Hague following his arrest in Manila on March 11, 2025.
In court, Duterte sat behind his defense team. In the few moments that the former official was shown in the livestream, he appeared to be listening intently.

Duterte had waived his personal appearance at the previous two status conferences. His appearance on Wednesday came as the ICC Trial Chamber discussed preparations for his trial, including the prosecution's witnesses and evidence, disclosure of materials to the defense, additional alleged incidents and the proposed trial schedule beginning Nov. 30.

He is facing three counts of crimes against humanity over alleged killings linked to his anti-drug campaign and other operations during his time as Davao City mayor and Philippine president. The ICC confirmed all three charges in April 2026, clearing the case to proceed to trial.
Duterte has denied wrongdoing and has maintained that killings during the drug war were carried out by police in self-defense.

Reuters earlier reported that prosecutors allege as many as 30,000 people may have been killed, while official police records put the number of suspects killed in police operations at about 6,200. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: EU’s von der Leyen backs AI slowdown, to invite frontier labs for talks
articles.summary: 'I will invite the main frontier labs for a discussion on how we can support ongoing industry efforts to pace the frontier,' Ursula von der Leyen says

blocks.text: URSULA VON DER LEYEN. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen reacts after delivering the State of the European Union address to the European Parliament, in Strasbourg, France, September 16, 2026.
Yves Herman/Reuters
'I will invite the main frontier labs for a discussion on how we can support ongoing industry efforts to pace the frontier,' Ursula von der Leyen says

STRASBOURG, France – European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Wednesday, September 16, backed calls by leading US AI labs for a pause in the development of the technology, saying she will invite the main frontier AI labs to discuss efforts to tackle the risks.

Von der Leyen’s comments in her annual speech to the European Parliament in Strasbourg came amid growing worries about the potential danger posed by artificial intelligence, putting her at odds with US President Donald Trump who has dismissed the AI safety alarm.

The dangers were underscored by Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon who resigned and accused both the company and OpenAI of ⁠racing toward self-improving superintelligence without acting responsibly. He had previously worked at OpenAI.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei last week called on AI companies to slow the rate at which they advance model capabilities, drawing the support of both Elon Musk, who runs xAI, and Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI.

“As the frontier models become more capable, these risks have come more sharply into focus. Models being developed will allow hacking on a level we never thought possible. And they will soon be in the hands of adversaries who see the world very differently from us,” von der Leyen told EU lawmakers.
She pointed to recent incidents of rogue AI agents and warnings from developers.

“CEOs of the most advanced companies tell us that it is time to slow down on the self-recursive models. To pace the frontier. If the people developing the technology are clear, then we should be too,” von der Leyen said.
Von der Leyen said landmark EU rules governing the use of AI adopted recently put Europe in the position to shape global efforts to tackle the risks.
She said Europe will work with like-minded partners such as Canada, the United Kingdom and others to take measures such as model evaluation, verification and AI security.
“I will invite the main frontier labs for a discussion on how we can support ongoing industry efforts to pace the frontier,” von der Leyen said.

She also proposed a social media ban for children under 13 and no personal accounts for people under the age of 15, saying that platforms have to prove that they are safe for children. She will announce details on Thursday. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Global Gender Gap Report: Women's hard-won gains 'fragile'
articles.summary: Two decades of progress toward gender parity is at risk as women's political representation declines, according to a new World Economic Forum report. At the current pace, the remaining gap could take…

image.caption: Women make up less than a third of lawmakers in the US CongressImage: J. Scott Applewhite/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The Global Gender Gap Report 2026, published by the World Economic Forum (WEF) on Wednesday, reveals that gender parity worldwide is closer than ever — standing at 69.2%.
However, the Geneva-based nonprofit warned that full parity may still be 120 years away and that the progress made so far remains "fragile."

The report, which looked at gender parity across workforce participation, education, health and politics in 145 economies, found that women now occupy senior leadership positions in government and business at levels that were rare globally when the index began in 2006.

Yet, while women's presence at the top of politics has grown since the first report, the past decade has seen that trend reverse. The percentage of countries led by women peaked in 2022 and has now fallen back to 2016 levels.
WEF Managing Director Saadia Zahidi warned that while parity is a foundation for growth and competitiveness, it is "not inevitable."

"To accelerate, governments and employers need to learn from the policies that work and apply them faster. A new economy demands a new approach to talent," Zahidi said in a press release to accompany the report.
Bangladesh lacks women in politics
Women still missing in top power roles

The WEF found that women remain underrepresented in roles with the largest economic and political influence. They still hold fewer than a fifth of chief executive officer (CEO) positions, while only one in 10 ministerial roles held by women is considered high influence.
While the number of ministerial roles led by women has risen 26% since 2008, only one in 10 was considered weighty then — a share the WEF report said was "virtually unchanged today."

Despite nearly $1 trillion (€866 billion) being invested globally to develop artificial intelligence (AI), the report also revealed that fewer than one in five AI engineers are women and they are underrepresented at every level of AI firms.

For the 17th consecutive year, Iceland leads the ranking with 93% of the gender gap closed, followed by its Nordic neighbors Finland and Norway. The three nations have made the Top 10, along with Sweden, every year since 2006.
Namibia ranked fourth globally, higher than Germany (9th), the United Kingdom (5th) and Australia (8th).
US falls in gender gap ranking
The United States dropped five places in the rankings to 47th, with 74.9% of its gender gap closed.
The country achieved full parity in education for a second year — ranking first in the world in that area.
In the US, women have long matched men in professional and technical jobs, but parity in senior management has fallen by almost 11 points since 2006, the WEF calculated.

The political score fell 4.1 points from last year after the share of women ministers dropped from two-thirds parity to one-half. The decline coincided with a lower share of women serving as Cabinet secretaries in President Donald Trump's second administration.
The WEF kept the head-of-state indicator for the US at zero as the world's largest economy has never had a female president.

blocks.caption: Only 63 of 193 countries, including Japan, have ever had a woman as head of government, according to the United NationsImage: Minoru Matsutani/Jiji Press/picture alliance

blocks.text: India stuck while China moves up
India, the world's most populous country, remains at 131st in the rankings, with 64.5% gender parity closed.

The report noted India's overall gains amount to a 4.3 percentage-point rise since 2006, which the authors said was mostly due to educational achievement. Women's labor-market participation has barely moved over 20 years, the WEF noted.

India's economic parity score has varied significantly since the first report. Parity among professional and technical workers has almost doubled since 2006, to 49.9%. Among legislators, senior officials and managers, however, it is still only 13.1%.

In parliament, India has closed 16.1% of the gender gap, up seven points since 2006, while the share of women in long-serving Prime Minister Narendra Modi's cabinet has fallen recently, with parity slipping to 5.9% from a 30% peak in 2019.

China, meanwhile, rose seven places to 96th, closing 69.9% of its gender gap. Economic parity is its strongest pillar, at 72.3%, but politics has barely moved in 20 years, with women still accounting for only a fraction of ministers.
Namibia's rise in women's political power
Large jumps for Namibia, Kenya and Ghana
Reaching 84.5% parity in the latest report, Namibia leads the way in Sub-Saharan Africa, climbing four places to No. 4 in the ranking.

Namibia has long been well represented by women on the political stage. Last year, Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah became its first female president. The country also has a female vice-president and the parliament speaker is a woman, too.
Other African countries were among the biggest climbers in the 2026 rankings, with Kenya rising 33 places in a year to 65th, Ghana up 32 places to 56th and Angola climbing 30 places to 87th.
However, Africa shows the widest range of outcomes for women, the report found, with Chad recording the lowest score of 57.8% parity closed.
Other large climbers in the 2026 report were Guatemala, which rose 31 points to 50th place, and the Czech Republic, which climbed 25 points to 77th.
The WEF also ranked the countries that have progressed the most since 2006 in closing gender gaps, namely Bolivia, Chile, Ecuador, France, Guatemala, Iceland, Mexico, Namibia and Nepal.

articles.title: New Orleans priest accused of abusing children in deaf community dies from apparent fall aged 87
articles.summary:
Archdiocese knew of allegations against Gerard Joseph ‘Jerry’ Howell for 40 years but continued to support him

A New Orleans…
articles.byline: Ramon Antonio Vargas and David Hammer of WWL Louisiana in New Orleans

blocks.text: A New Orleans Catholic priest whose prolific sexual abuse of children in the local deaf community was known for at least four decades by the city’s archdiocese without meaningful consequence has died after evidently falling in his Texas apartment.

Gerard Joseph “Jerry” Howell, 87, was found dead at about 5pm on 8 September by Austin police department officers who were responding to a welfare check on the block listed for the senior living community where he had been residing, the agency said in a statement. The statement – which didn’t name Howell but was provided when police were asked about his death specifically – said first responders had gone to the block to investigate a report that an 87-year-old individual had fallen.
Local emergency medical services personnel soon arrived to provide medical aid to that individual, but he stopped breathing and was pronounced dead at the scene, police said.
The Austin medical examiner’s office was still working to determine the cause of death in the case on Tuesday, but it was “not being investigated as a homicide”, police said.

New Orleans’ Roman Catholic archdiocese provided support to Howell for 40 years after becoming aware of his serial child molestation. They kept him on as an active priest even after reporting him to law enforcement in 1980 and his being publicly exposed by WWL Louisiana in 1992, and then paying him his retirement benefits until at least 2020.

A church spokesperson said the archdiocese learned of Howell’s death later that same week. And an archdiocese-managed webpage of dozens of priests and deacons who were removed from ministry for abuse of a minor was then quietly updated to list him as deceased.
One of Howell’s most outspoken survivors, Kathleen Austin, said on Tuesday that it was a relief for her to learn of his death.

blocks.caption: Kathleen Austin in God as My Witness. Photograph: Courtesy of filmmakers Lindsay Quinn Pitre and Michael Brandne Sr

blocks.text: “He will no longer be able to harm another innocent child,” Austin said. “I can now relax, not worrying about where he is [or] what he’s doing.”
Efforts to contact Howell’s family for comment were not immediately successful.
Howell’s death is significant because his case was in the public eye for decades while he continued to avoid punishment for abuse he inflicted while ministering to people with impaired hearing.

WWL, a Guardian reporting partner, was rolling cameras when Austin confronted him at his home in Texas all the way back in 1992. The news station reported that the archdiocese of New Orleans was aware of many of Howell’s alleged child-abuse victims by then and refused to remove him from active ministry.

Records later obtained by the Guardian showed the then New Orleans archbishop, Philip Hannan, reported Howell to the devoutly Catholic district attorney, Harry Connick Sr, in 1980. Connick, though, never charged Howell.

Other records showed the next archbishop, Francis Schulte, told Howell to “quit and get a job” after the WWL report in 1992. But Howell appealed to global Catholic leaders at the Vatican, who ordered Schulte to let him “continue as a priest with full financial benefits”.

And the records show the New Orleans archdiocese sent Howell for mental health treatment in 2010, with a psychologist diagnosing him as “high risk” and reporting the church was aware of at least 24 child victims.

Still, the archdiocese continued to quietly support Howell in his retirement, paying his full living expenses, insurance and a $650 monthly stipend. Those benefits stayed in place until a federal judge halted them in 2020, after the archdiocese filed for federal bankruptcy protection amid the financial fallout of the worldwide, decades-old Catholic clergy sexual molestation scandal.

Yet not even that totally cut Howell off from support by the New Orleans archdiocese. WWL and the Guardian found a 2020 letter that the then New Orleans archbishop, Gregory Aymond, wrote to a Vatican official, calling the bankruptcy court’s cancellation of Howell’s benefits along with those of other archdiocesan clergy abusers “unjust and painful”. The outlets also reported that Aymond had directed Howell to seek aid from a non-profit dedicated to helping priests prohibited from ministering.
The leader of that particular group, the Men of Melchizedek, had headed a separate organization which was previously shut down for misusing donations and misleading donors about its purpose.
Aymond retired in February and was succeeded as New Orleans archbishop by James Checchio.

The archdiocese’s website discloses that Howell, ordained in 1964, was named as the offender in nine claims of sexually abusive or grooming behavior filed as part of its bankruptcy. Immediately before Howell’s death, that was the second most among eight living clergymen on the archdiocese’s list of those removed from ministry for abuse of a minor.

About 740 clergy molestation claimants are divvying up a $305m settlement that the archdiocese agreed to pay to resolve its bankruptcy protection case, with individuals’ compensation amounts based on a complicated rubric meant to assess various factors such as the nature and duration of the abuse involved.
Many of those claimants name abusers whom the archdiocese has not included in its list of clergy removed from ministry for abuse of a minor.

As of the day after Howell’s death, 14 claimants had requested reconsideration of their allocated amounts, and about 220 had indicated they would not contest them, according to a bankruptcy court filing on Monday providing an update on the disbursement of the settlement.

The New Orleans archdiocese is among 44 US Catholic religious institutions to have filed for bankruptcy protection in the course of the worldwide church’s clergy abuse scandal – and among 29 to settle such a legal proceeding, according to information compiled by Penn State University’s law school.
A spokesperson for the archdiocese said it never restarted Howell’s retirement benefits once they were discontinued, even after the bankruptcy settlement.

Howell’s abuse of Austin during her childhood was one of several clergy abuse cases studied by the award-winning 2025 documentary film God As My Witness, which scrutinizes the New Orleans archdiocese’s bankruptcy. For one of the film’s most striking moments, Austin recounts meeting with Hannan to discuss Howell’s abuse of her – only to be directed to “kick him in the balls” the next time she saw him.
Austin, who grew up with parents and a sister who were hearing impaired, told film-makers Lindsay Quinn Pitre and Michael Brandner Sr that she was shocked by that guidance.
“I remember looking at him thinking, ‘Really? This is how you handle this?’” Austin says in the film, which recently became available on streaming. “‘That’s not my job. This is your job.’”

On Tuesday, Austin described having empathy for relatives of Howell, whose late brother and fellow priest Rodney is also considered by church officials to be credibly accused of child molestation. They “had to live with two pedophile priests and the terror that … they inflicted”.
Yet Austin added that, to her, Howell’s apparently becoming one of the more than 43,000 people in the US who die from falls annually on average fittingly was “a miserable way to go”.
“His death … puts me at rest, and when he meets our maker, hopefully … his punishment far exceeds what he did to children while he was here on the planet,” Austin remarked.

articles.title: [Be The Good] Holding space through Civic Circles
articles.summary: This is how we show up for our readers, our partners, and the communities impacted by the stories we cover. We hope you can be part of it.

blocks.text: Hi, I’m Jene Pangue, Head of MovePH, Rappler’s civic engagement arm.

During our recent Civic Circles initiative, I stood near one of our workshop tables when a mother quietly reached out to hand me a small, handcrafted whistle. Jennifer shared that her son had experienced bullying at school. Desperate for help, she had reached out to authorities, only to be met with silence.

Finding a community that held space for her story allowed her to feel less alone. That whistle, which she was giving away for free, became a tangible reminder encouraging others in the room to keep speaking up so that no family has to face these struggles in isolation.

I also met Teacher Mars, a public school educator of 20 years who traveled all the way from Laguna to join us. Despite the heavy demands of her daily work, she was eager to learn how to keep children and schools safe. “Ang teacher ngayon dapat matatag at matibay,” she said. “Ang dami naming ginagawa na labas na sa responsibilidad namin. Pero hanggang kaya, kakayanin.” (Today’s teachers must be strong and resilient. We do so many things that are outside our responsibilities. But as long as we can, we will endure.)

Their stories reflect a broader problem. Across the country, communities are grappling with rising campus violence, critical resource shortages, and a mounting mental health crisis. Teachers are often forced to act as unequipped first responders, while parents navigate painful realities in silence.

To help address these challenges, MovePH envisioned a space where citizens from all walks of life — educators, parents, youth advocates, civil society leaders or ordinary citizens who care — could come together, move beyond online discussions, and co-create actionable solutions.
This is the heart of how Civic Circles came to life.

Our pilot session brought together over 50 in-person participants from child rights groups, academe, local government units, healthcare, law enforcement, and parent associations, alongside hundreds more who joined virtually.

We opened with a panel discussion featuring Quezon City Councilor Aly Medalla, National Police Anti-Cybercrime Group spokesperson Captain Wallen Arancillo, Philippine Pediatric Society Child Protection specialist Dr. Princess Gairanod, and Department of Education (DepEd) Director IV Razzel Anne Requesto. They underscored that boosting funding and strengthening systemic responses are essential to creating lasting safety.

The panelists also highlighted the importance of active parental involvement, localized safety frameworks, trauma-informed drills, expanded mental health support, and enhanced cybersecurity capacity. You can watch the full panel discussion here.
Building on these insights, participants rotated across four action station circles to translate ideas into practical steps.
Their recommendations include the following:

items: boosting campus security through parent-teacher capacity building;
strengthening psychosocial care through regular counseling, parent internet safety orientations, and safe spaces — alongside commitments to expand licensed support and referral system;
tackling systemic violence via interagency policy collaboration; and
mitigating digital safety risks through community-wide awareness campaigns on parental control tools and cybersecurity advocacy.

blocks.text: We thank our co-organizers, CyberGuardiansPH, and Mental Health Youth Hub. Their technical expertise, support, and dedication to youth well-being were essential in bringing this multisectoral and trauma-informed space to life.
To ensure these conversations extend beyond event-day, participants and community members can stay connected and join upcoming initiatives through our education chatroom on the app.

MovePH will continue working alongside our partner groups and volunteers to consolidate these commitments into actionable briefs or community toolkits that concerned citizens like Jennifer and Teacher Mars can bring directly to their schools, homes, and local councils.
Is there a specific commitment or solution from this session that you would like to support? Or a topic you think we should tackle in our next Civic Circles?
We are just getting started, and we would love to have you with us.
Civic Circles: How can we keep our children and schools safe?
Organized in partnership with CyberGuardiansPH and Mental Health Youth Hub, this pilot initiative tackles rising school violence and digital risks

articles.title: Saudis pound Yemen as Houthis solidify gains in new theater of Middle East war
articles.summary: Traders say a prolonged closure of Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline could cut off as much as 4% of global oil supply

blocks.text: Iran-aligned Houthi fighters pose next to a captured vehicle following what the source described as an attack on Saudi-backed forces in the location given by the source as al Jawf governorate, Yemen, in this screengrab taken from a video released by Houthi Military Media on September 15, 2026.
HOUTHI MILITARY MEDIA/Handout via REUTERS
Traders say a prolonged closure of Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline could cut off as much as 4% of global oil supply

items: Saudi warplanes intensified airstrikes on Yemen as the Iran-backed Houthis made significant territorial gains, raising concerns over global oil supply disruptions.
The United States issued a travel warning for Saudi Arabia and acknowledged the potential for a worsening global energy crisis due to the conflict's escalation.
Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince sought military support from President Trump, who faces a dilemma between risking further US involvement or allowing the Houthi advance to exacerbate the energy crisis.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Saudi warplanes pounded Yemen, the Houthis said on Wednesday, September 16, as the Iran-backed fighters solidified their gains after a lightning advance that has extended Tehran’s reach in the Middle East war and further disrupted global oil supplies.

In a sign of the worsening conflict in a new theatre, the United States tightened its travel warning for Saudi Arabia, banning government employees from travelling within 20 miles of the Yemen border.

The Houthis, who since last week have swept through Yemeni towns along the Red Sea coast and seized islands in the Bab el-Mandeb strait at its mouth, released battlefield video overnight of fighters seizing armoured vehicles from Saudi-backed forces. Warplanes flew overhead and huge explosions billowed into the sky from desert dunes.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the Houthis had shot down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet. No immediate evidence was presented and Saudi officials did not immediately respond to emails seeking comment.

Saree said the Saudis had carried out as many as 450 air strikes on Yemen this week. Officials in the Saudi-backed government that controls southern Yemen have acknowledged that their forces and those of Saudi Arabia were conducting air strikes on Houthi positions, though Riyadh itself has not confirmed them.

The Houthis have fired repeatedly into Saudi Arabia over the past week causing alarms over cities in the south and west. An attack blamed on Iran-aligned fighters in Iraq last week also knocked out Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, the main route used to divert exports away from the blockaded Strait of Hormuz.

Riyadh said its air defenses had shot down a Houthi drone south of Mecca on Tuesday before it entered prohibited airspace over the holy city, an attack it said crossed a “red line” of threatening shrines sacred to all Muslims. Houthi spokesperson Saree denied the group had targeted Mecca, and said the Saudi reports were a set-up for propaganda purposes.

The extension of the war into Yemen threatens to worsen the global energy supply shortage caused by the six-month-old US-Israeli war on Iran, which has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

The price of Brent crude hovered around $108 a barrel on Wednesday, close to its highest level since May. The politically sensitive average retail price of diesel fuel in the United States hit another all-time high above $6.30 a gallon for the first time.

Traders say a prolonged closure of Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline could cut off as much as 4% of global oil supply. Saudi Arabia has not said when operations might resume, but US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC on Tuesday that crude oil should be flowing through the pipeline within days.

Saudi Arabia has led a coalition battling the Houthis since 2015. The conflict had largely quietened under a ceasefire in recent years, but reignited when the Houthis declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia in July and fired at southern areas in the kingdom. Violence has intensified sharply this month when the militant group pushed back forces aligned with the Saudi-backed internationally recognised Yemeni government.
Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman phoned US President Donald Trump last week seeking military support, which so far has been limited to intelligence aid.
The United States bombed the Houthis for two months in 2025, but halted that campaign after reaching what President Donald Trump described as a ceasefire with the group.

Trump now faces a dilemma of whether to stand by and risk the Houthi advance worsening the global energy crisis, or provide more direct military support to the Saudis and risk extending the costly US intervention to another theater. – Rappler.com

The Sandiganbayan Third Division on Wednesday denied the bid of former House Speaker and Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez to be transferred to hospital detention, saying other persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) are in worse health conditions than him.
“We would like to emphasize that invocation of ill health is not sufficient for an accused’s continued confinement in the hospital,” Sandiganbayan Third Division chairperson Karl Miranda said.
Romualdez is detained at the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas in connection with a P7.4-billion plunder case.
He entered his not guilty plea to the charge via videoconferencing, as allowed by the Sandiganbayan.
The anti-graft court also noted that Romualdez’s health condition was found to be stable by doctors from the state-run Philippine General Hospital (PGH) during a court-ordered medical examination.
In his motion dated September 14, Romualdez sought confinement at the Veterans Memorial Medical Center.
Romualdez’s counsel, lawyer Ade Fajardo, said they would still avail themselves of legal remedies following the court’s decision if they deemed it necessary.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Prosecution to call Sebastian Duterte to witness stand in VP Sara’s trial
articles.summary: The prosecution wants to ask Sebastian Duterte about Davao City hall's dealings with Gencorp, of which the Vice President is a stockholder

blocks.text: BASTE. Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte.
Facebook/ Baste Duterte
The prosecution wants to ask Sebastian Duterte about Davao City hall's dealings with Gencorp, of which the Vice President is a stockholder
MANILA, Philippines – The prosecution team in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte will call her brother, Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte, to the witness stand.
The impeachment court on Wednesday, September 16, granted the prosecution’s request to compel the attendance of the younger Duterte on September 23.

“In broad strokes, we remember that in the SALNs (Statements of Assets Liabilities and Net worth), it was mentioned that among the companies she has financial interest… is Gencorp,” prosecution spokesman Jay Tolosa said.
“We want to know, in his capacity as mayor of Davao, if Gencorp has dealings with the city government of Davao,” he added.

The younger Duterte was not initially identified as a witness by the prosecution team in its pre-trial brief, although it is not precluded from asking him to testify as among the unnamed, reserve witnesses.

The development comes a day after Rappler published an exclusive report detailing how Gencorp cornered P15 million in food and catering contracts from the PhilHealth Davao Regional Office and Davao City Hall between 2022 and 2025.
Sara, who is a stockholder of the company, was already vice president at the time.

The Constitution bars a vice president’s participation in any business, and the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Official instructs them to divest their shares from any private business enterprise within 60 days from their assumption. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Ladbrokes owner prepares to cut 400 jobs weeks after profit boost
articles.summary:
Entain, which also owns Coral and BetMGM, starts consultation process over customer care roles

The Ladbrokes owner, Entain, has said it is preparing to cut 400 jobs, only weeks after the…

blocks.text: The Ladbrokes owner, Entain, has said it is preparing to cut 400 jobs, only weeks after the FTSE 100 business reported better than expected profit in its first half of the year.
The gambling group, which also owns Coral and BetMGM, has started a consultation process that could remove one in five of its 2,000 customer care jobs.

Its chief executive, Stella David, said the proposed changes were made to ensure the “business remains competitive, financially resilient, and well positioned for the future as our sector faces an increasingly challenging operating environment.
“This decision has not been made lightly, and our immediate priority is to support those of our colleagues who may be impacted through this transition.”

It comes only weeks after the company revealed its underlying operating profit had hit £479m in the six months to the end of June – 2% below the same period in the year prior but ahead of what investors had expected.
Entain blamed the job cuts partly on higher taxes in the UK, as the sector also braces for a mooted increase to machine games duty in the budget.
The chancellor, John Healey, is reportedly looking at increasing the levy in his inaugural budget on 28 October, in a way that could target betting shops and adult gaming centres (AGCs).
AGCs, which offer 24-hour gambling machines, have grown rapidly across UK high streets in recent years, disproportionately targeting economically deprived areas.
While online casinos were hit with a tax increase in Rachel Reeves’s budget last year, duty on physical slot machines in AGCs were not affected.

Doubling machine games duty could increase the tax take from “category B” £2-a-spin slot machines by between £275m and £458m, on top of the £600m they currently pay, according to research by the Social Market Foundation thinktank.

David wrote to Andy Burnham last week, arguing that doubling the standard rate of machine games duty from 20% to 40% would add about £100m to the cost of running Entain’s retail business in the UK, and claiming that could result in 1,470 betting shop closures in the UK and 15,900 job losses.
after newsletter promotion
Burnham has previously backed a proposal by Gordon Brown to pay for an end to the two-child benefit cap by tapping the gambling industry for more tax.

Entain, which is headquartered in London and employs more than 28,000 people worldwide, started as GVC Holdings in 2004 under Kenny Alexander. It has grown into one of the biggest betting businesses in the world, and includes brands such as BetCity and Eurobet as well as gaming brands Foxy Bingo, Gala and PartyCasino.
Shares in the company, which will be demoted to the mid-cap FTSE 250 index from 21 September, are down by about 36% in the year to date. They fell 1% in early trading on Wednesday.

articles.title: Marcos looked beyond politics in appointing ex-Duterte supporter RJ Nieto — Palace
articles.summary: Former pro-Duterte vlogger RJ Nieto now holds a Cabinet position under Marcos administration.

blocks.text: September 16, 2026 | 5:44pm

MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang explained on Wednesday, September 16, that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. set politics aside in appointing Rey Joseph “RJ” Nieto, a former supporter of the Dutertes, to a Cabinet position.

Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said during a press briefing that Marcos looked beyond Nieto’s past affiliation with the Dutertes in assigning him a role directly under the Office of the President.
“Even before, sinabi po natin na ang pangulo po ay hindi tumitingin sa kulay,” Castro said. (Even before, we have said that the president does not look at political colors.)
The former pro-Duterte vlogger behind the deactivated Thinking Pinoy blog was appointed assistant secretary at the Office of the Cabinet Secretary earlier Wednesday.
Castro said Marcos can appoint anyone to the government as long as such a person will serve the public first and not the people they previously supported.

“Kung kayo po ay makikitang magiging asset sa gobyerno para mas maging maganda ang serbisyo ng isang ahensya, hindi po mag-aatubili ang pangulo na kayo ay kunin,” Castro said. “Provided na ang puso po ninyo kahit ano ang inyong kulay dapat ay sa taong bayan at sa bansa, hindi sa isang tao o sa isang dati niyong tinataguyod.”

(If you are seen as an asset to the government to improve the service of an agency, the president will not hesitate to bring you on board. Provided that your heart, regardless of your political colors, is for the people and the country, not for one individual you previously supported.)
Castro had not disclosed the specific tasks that come with Nieto’s role yet, but noted that he will most likely be involved in delivering services to Filipinos in far-flung areas.
“Definitely alam naman natin kung anong pinakatrabaho ng CabSec. Ito ay para mas maabot ‘yung ating mga kababayan sa mas pinakasulok pa na parte ng Pilipinas,” Castro said.
(We definitely know what the job of the CabSec is. That is to reach our fellow countrymen from the most remote areas in the Philippines.)

articles.summary: International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III Presiding Judge Joanna Korner on Wednesday advised the prosecution in former President Rodrigo Duterte"s crimes against humanity case to think…

blocks.text: Published September 16, 2026 5:42pm

Former Philippines president Rodrigo Duterte appears before the International Criminal Court, as the court hears arguments regarding Duterte's health and ability to stand trial, while he faces murder charges related to his war on drugs, in The Hague, Netherlands, September 16 2026. REUTERS/Piroschka van de Wouw/Pool

International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III Presiding Judge Joanna Korner on Wednesday advised the Prosecution in former President Rodrigo Duterte’s crimes against humanity case to think about reducing the number of their witnesses.
The judge said the prosecution requested 193 hours to present its case, which she said was a "very lengthy period of time."
“You may want to think about whether it is possible to reduce the number of witnesses, as I say,” Korner said during the third status conference.
Korner noted that the prosecution has four experts on the same topic.
“It really is important… that we conclude the case as quickly as possible. I think you may want to think long and hard about this,” she said.
For their part, ICC trial lawyer Edward Jeremy said the prosecution will look for opportunities to streamline their case.
Jeremy said their request for 193 hours was already the “reduced version.”
Korner, meanwhile, clarified that the Trial Chamber will not make a decision today.
Duterte, who is is facing charges over alleged killings during his time as President and Davao City mayor, attended his status conference for the first time.
He was arrested in March 2025 at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Terminal 3.
The former Philippine leader is currently detained at the ICC Detention Centre in Scheveningen in The Hague, The Netherlands. — RSJ, GMA News
